name: Saint Lawrence
history: One of the seven deacons of Rome, Lawrence cared for the Church’s goods and its poor. He was martyred in 258 under the Emperor Valerian, a few days after his bishop, Pope Sixtus II. His courage made him one of the best-loved martyrs of Rome, and his name is said in the Roman Canon.
life: When Valerian ordered the execution of bishops, priests and deacons, Pope Sixtus II was beheaded on 6 August 258. Tradition, recorded by Saint Ambrose, says that Lawrence followed the pope to his death, asking why he should be left behind, and that Sixtus told him he would follow in three days. The prefect of Rome demanded the treasures of the Church. Lawrence asked for time, gathered the poor, the sick and the widows whom the Church supported, and presented them: these are the treasure of the Church. Tradition holds that he was roasted on a gridiron and, with astonishing calm, told his executioners to turn him over, for one side was done. He was buried on the Via Tiburtina, where the basilica of San Lorenzo fuori le Mura now stands. The Perseid meteors of early August are called in Italy the tears of Saint Lawrence.
prayerTo: Saint Lawrence, deacon and martyr, you saw the face of Christ in the poor and called them the treasure of the Church. Pray that I may serve them gladly and not be ashamed of them. Give me some of your courage and good humour when I suffer for what is right. Amen.
penance: Give generously to the poor today, in money, food or time, as Lawrence gave the Church’s goods away rather than see them seized.
meditation: These are the treasure of the Church. Who are the poor in your own street or parish, and do you see them as treasure or as a burden?
prayer: Grant us, we beseech You, almighty God, to extinguish the flames of our sins, as You granted St. Lawrence to overcome the fires of his tortures. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
